verdicts.reason: The three-layer split (obs / spine / labels) is sound and lazy, but as specified the tables cannot carry an unbiased estimator. Three concrete gaps. (1) `silver/flood_obs` admits only observations that ASSERT flooding, so there is no channel for an observed-dry reading — FloodNet below threshold and CO-OPS below threshold are the only uncontaminated negatives available anywhere in this source set, and D1's schema makes them unrepresentable. D5's negatives are therefore locked to 'no report' by the shape of D1, not by choice. (2) `gold/flood_labels` carries per-EVENT coverage flags (D3) but no per-ASSET detectability field. Two assets with identical true flooding have different P(label=1) depending on whether a FloodNet sensor is within 50 m, whether a station name is parseable, and whether the block reports 311 — and that detectability is correlated with elevation, borough, and asset type. That is differential outcome misclassification correlated with the covariates, which biases coefficients in either direction, not toward the null, so it cannot be waved off as 'noise'. (3) `ref/flood_events` is placed in `ref/`, which pipeline-02/09 uses for FROZEN reference (grids, cells, zones, cell_pixel, calendar, picks). This spine is threshold-derived from a mutable 311 archive that back-fills and re-geocodes; rebuilding it next month silently changes every label and every published CSI, with no way to tell. Pipeline-09 already solved exactly this with `pick_id = zip sha1`.
verdicts.amendment: Add `obs_kind` in {wet, dry, unknown} to `silver/flood_obs` so below-threshold FloodNet/CO-OPS readings land as first-class dry observations. Add to `gold/flood_labels` a per-row `detect_mask` (bitfield: which label-grade sources could have seen THIS asset in THIS window — FloodNet in radius and reporting, station name parseable, 311 catchment active) plus `n_obs_by_source`. Move the spine to `silver/flood_events` and stamp every `gold/flood_labels` row with `label_version` = sha1 of (311 as-of date, alert as-of date, threshold parameters, radii); keep `ref/` for frozen reference only.

verdicts.reason: Refuted twelve ways on the draft's own measurements. (i) The era split fits noise: era-1 p99=97, era-2=84, bootstrap 95% CIs [85,113] and [68,133], difference 13 with 95% CI [-36,+37] and P(era2>=era1)=0.29. There is no measurable era drift at p99 to absorb. (ii) A rank threshold cannot express what it is being asked to: per-era p99 yields 34 era-1 and 23 era-2 event-days = 3.4/yr in BOTH eras by construction, even though era 2 holds the three largest days in the record (912, 634, 364/351). The rule defines away the exact change it claims to correct for. (iii) The drift that IS real is ignored: weekend daily mean is 0.546x weekday (95% CI [0.474,0.630]), zero-days 19.9% vs 5.8%, weekend p99 78 vs weekday 97. Storms do not avoid weekends. Under one threshold a Saturday storm needs ~25% more physical severity to become an event-day; criterion-(a) days come out 19.3% weekend vs the 28.6% calendar share. (iv) The quantile is unjustified and the spine is 3x sensitive to it: q=0.985/0.99/0.995 -> 83/57/28 event-days, and the sign of the era adjustment flips (84<97 at q=0.99, 150>126 at q=0.995) — proof the era term is estimating tail noise from ~23-34 points. (v) p99 is computed over days with >=1 complaint, dropping 486 zero-days in era 1 (13.3%) and 108 in era 2 (5.4%) — asymmetric conditioning contaminating the very era comparison being made. (vi) 19/57 criterion-(a) event-days are Dec-Mar (2011-01-18, 2014-02-05/13/14, 2016-02-08/16, 2018-03-02, 2018-12-21...) — snowmelt/ice/frozen-basin ponding, all classed `pluvial`, while pipeline-08 already carries `t2m_c` and a rain-not-snow convention the flood spine drops. (vii) Criterion (b) has no threshold at all: of 36 alert first-seen days, 27 have no 311 spike, and 2021-05-23 has 1 alert event with ZERO citywide street/highway flooding complaints (2020-05-28: 1; 2022-03-02 and 2023-07-08: 3; 2023-08-29: 3 complaints against 4 alert events). `research/subway-flood-labels.md` already measured that some matches are boilerplate flood footers (Ida event_ids 29827/29853) and 0.8% are flood-MITIGATION planned work. These near-empty days are 27 of the union's 50 era-2 events, each contributing ~1 positive against the full asset universe. (viii) The window is defined by the label: 'union of contributing observation timestamps +/-3h' guarantees every label-grade observation is inside its own window (edge POD = 1 by construction) and makes window length a monotone function of label count, so any window-aggregated precip feature is mechanically larger for events with more labels — a direct label-to-feature leakage path. (ix) Day assignment is wrong for a quarter of alert events: 24/99 are first seen 00:00-05:59 local (Ida's system-wide alert 02:31 on 09-02, for rain that fell the evening of 09-01), and 311 `created_date` is the filing time, not the incident time. The +/-3h pad is smaller than the lag, so the window lands after the rain. (x) Local-calendar-day bucketing of a COUNT threshold means an overnight storm splitting 45/45 across midnight fires neither day while an identical daytime storm fires. (xi) Class logic hole: 'coastal if (d) without (a)' classifies a Storm-Events flash-flood day or a subway-flood day that coincides with a spring tide as coastal; 'mixed if both' is only defined for (a) AND (d). (xii) Coastal coverage gap: Battery and Kings Point only. Jamaica Bay/Rockaway has no gauge in the set yet is among the most flood-prone coastal areas (FloodNet's own largest sampled event is `Q - Beach 84 St`, 17.72 in) — Rockaway coastal events are systematically non-events.
verdicts.amendment: Replace the p99 rule with a physically-anchored, drift-corrected trigger and a forcing-defined window. (a) becomes: daily count exceeds k x expected(day), where expected(day) is a negative-binomial offset fit on non-event days with a smooth year term (not a 2-era step), day-of-week, and month; fire on standardized excess > k (start k=4, sweep once, publish the sweep). One threshold for the whole record; drift lives in the offset, not the threshold. Evaluate on a rolling 24h window ending each hour, not the local calendar day. (b) becomes: >=1 subway flood event NAMING >=1 station via ticket 02's extractor, excluding boilerplate flood-reminder footers and `flood protection|mitigation|barrier|resiliency` rows; a single unnamed system-wide alert does not make an event-day. Add a phase gate: an event-day is `pluvial` only if the Cell-hour spine shows liquid precip in the 24h window with `t2m_c` above freezing; otherwise class `snowmelt`, kept in the table and excluded from pluvial training/validation. Build the window from the FORCING, never from observations: [first hour with >=1 mm citywide, last hour with >=1 mm] + 6h drain, hour-aligned; coastal = the contiguous above-threshold tide run +/-3h. Class rule: coastal iff (d) and no pluvial forcing; pluvial iff pluvial forcing and no (d); mixed iff both; add `snowmelt` and `unclassified`. Add a Jamaica Bay/Rockaway coastal source or record the blind spot as a per-event coverage flag.

verdicts.reason: The spine-only assignment (Storm Events, CO-OPS at county/zone grain never attaching to assets) holds and I cannot break it. The label-grade and covariate assignments do not. (i) FloodNet is simultaneously label-grade truth here and a feature source in ticket 08 ('FloodNet-derived priors from 03'). A sensor exceedance sets flooded=1 on every asset in its Cell and within 50 m; a FloodNet-derived prior is a feature on those same assets. The high-confidence tier 08 will headline its CSI on is the tier with the most direct leakage. (ii) FloodNet truth is not a random sample: the network is deliberately sited at flood-prone blocks, coverage grows monotonically from 1 sensor (2020-10-05) to 440 and still adding (latest 2026-08-13, nine days before the research pull), and pre-Nov-2021 sensors sampled at 5 min not 60 s — so Ida, the highest-value event, has both the coarsest sampling and the thinnest network. Labels-per-event rise over the record from instrument count alone, and a temporal split will show the model 'improving' for that reason. (iii) FloodNet negatives are documented non-dry: the access doc states sensors mount on signposts 'not necessarily at the true topographic low point' and sidewalk-mounted units 'can't detect roadbed flooding until water rises above curb height'. The one source that could supply true dry observations under-reports by design. (iv) NFIP as 'chronic exposure prior' is near-circular with the Sandy-polygon label: NFIP claims exist essentially only where flood insurance is held, which is driven by the FEMA SFHA mandatory-purchase rule, and the Sandy inundation polygon is approximately the SFHA. Predicting Sandy inundation from NFIP claim density is predicting the flood zone from the flood zone — coastal CSI will look excellent and mean nothing. (v) '311 sewer backup + catch basin (chronic background)' is not a covariate, it is a label proxy: measured on the draft's own pulls, daily SA vs SJ+SH counts correlate r=0.639 raw / 0.576 log1p over 5,462 shared days, and the draft itself notes the same storms top both lists. A chronic SA-density feature encodes the same reporting propensity that generates the SJ label, so the model learns who calls 311. (vi) Sandy inundation polygons attached by `contains` will produce more positive asset-event pairs than every other event combined (a citywide coastal polygon x every entrance/stop/segment inside it, vs dozens per ordinary event). With Sandy in training it owns the loss; with Sandy held out the model has almost no coastal positives left. No capping or per-event weighting rule exists. (vii) The Sandy polygon has no time resolution — it is a maximum-extent surface, so the +/-3h event window is fiction for it and it cannot participate in any within-event timing analysis.
verdicts.amendment: Per source, choose truth OR feature, never both, and record the choice as an `obs_role` column so 08 cannot silently reuse it: either FloodNet exceedance is truth and every FloodNet-derived feature is barred from the model, or FloodNet is a feature and validation runs on HWM + alerts only. Build NFIP and 311-sewer-backup features with a strict as-of cutoff (claims/complaints strictly before the event window start), acknowledge their FEMA-zone and reporting-propensity content, and report the score with and without them. Move Sandy polygons to a separate `flood_extent` layer used only as a held-out coastal sanity check, never mixed into asset-event training positives; if kept, apply a per-event positive weight 1/n_positives_in_event so no event exceeds a stated share of the positive mass. Add an `observed_dry` role for below-threshold FloodNet/CO-OPS readings with an explicit note that FloodNet dry means 'dry above curb height at the signpost', not 'dry'.

verdicts.reason: The dedupe half is measured-correct and I cannot break it: event_id post-2020 / status_id pre-2020, union across all updates recovering the 19% of events that acquire flood wording after update 0. The attachment half breaks four ways. (i) Incoherent spatial support inside one binary column: FloodNet attaches to 'its own street segment/Cell' — H3 res 8 is ~0.74 km2 — while 311 and HWM attach at 100 m (~0.03 km2). One sensor blankets a 25x larger area than one 311 report, so `flooded` is a union of detectors whose support differs by more than an order of magnitude. Worse, the Cell is also the precip feature unit, so a Cell-blanket label is deterministic given the sensor and the model can memorize cell_id. (ii) Entrance grain is fake: 'alert station label -> that station's entrances directly' makes the label constant across all entrances of a station, so it has ZERO within-station variance. Ticket 07 builds entrance-level features (DSM-DEM stairwell flag, sill elevation) that this label can never validate, and scoring 2,120 entrances against 472-station labels reports a ~4.5x inflated n — station-grain skill wearing entrance-grain clothes. (iii) The alert source's station yield is ANTI-correlated with event severity: the research measured that during Ida and 2023-09-29 a large share of alerts are deliberately system-wide ('across the region', 'across New York City') with no station named, and Ida's 29 events are mostly per-line system-wide messages. The two events carrying half the positive mass (49/99) name the fewest stations, so the alert label is weakest exactly where flooding was worst. (iv) 'Sensitivity-swept in 08's validation' is threshold tuning on the evaluation set unless the sweep runs inside each CV fold; and a fixed 100 m radius attaches roughly an order of magnitude more assets per report in midtown than on Staten Island, so label density varies by borough for reasons unrelated to water.
verdicts.amendment: Drop the 'own Cell' clause: FloodNet attaches at a single stated radius (start 100 m, matching 311/HWM) so all point sources share one support; if a Cell-grain label is wanted make it a separate `cell_labels` table, never mixed into asset labels. Make station the label grain for alert-derived labels and carry entrance rows with `label_support='station'` so 08 must aggregate to station or exclude them; entrance-grain claims require an entrance-grain truth source (FloodNet/HWM/photo), stated as such. Add a `system_wide` flag on alert events with no parseable station and exclude those events from station-grain POD denominators rather than silently scoring them all-negative. State that the radius sweep runs inside the fold and that the reported CSI is the outer-loop number, with the full sweep published rather than the argmax. Define `count-weighted presence` or delete it — the label as written is binary, so the weight currently has no consumer.

verdicts.reason: (i) The severity tier is not a severity measure. max(FloodNet depth > HWM > alert > 311) orders by SOURCE, so a 12 mm FloodNet reading outranks a high-water mark recording 1.5 m. Which source covers an asset is a function of sensor siting and station-name parseability, so the ordinal is confounded with coverage; and because FloodNet coverage grows 2020->2026, mean severity tier drifts upward over the record from instrument count alone. Any model trained or validated on tiers learns coverage. (ii) The negative set cannot support CSI/POD/FAR. flooded=0 means 'no source reported' = 'not flooded OR not observed' — a positive-unlabeled problem. FAR is inflated by every unreported true flood; POD is deflated by unreported floods inside positive events; and the contamination rate varies by borough, hour, day-of-week (measured weekend/weekday reporting ratio 0.546, CI [0.474,0.630]) and year. The numbers 08 publishes are therefore not FAR and POD for flooding; they are FAR and POD for 'predict a 311 report'. Documenting the caveat does not make the estimator unbiased. (iii) The estimand is never named — P(asset floods | forcing) vs P(a report is generated | forcing) differ by the reporting propensity, and only the second is estimable from this label set as designed. (iv) Deferring to '08 owns tiered-truth handling' is not available: every correction 08 would need — an observed-dry channel, a per-asset detectability mask, a propensity offset or case-control design — is TABLE SHAPE, and this is the ticket that fixes the shape. (v) Rare-event arithmetic is never stated: post-2020 the union of (a) and (b) is 50 event-days, 49 of 99 subway events sit on 2 days, and 26 of 36 alert-days carry exactly 1 event. Under event-held-out CV the effective independent sample is ~36-50 clusters dominated by two, so a 5-fold split has one fold with ~30x the positives of the others and CSI will swing by tenths between folds. Pipeline-10 already established 'errors clustered by wet event'; the flood label set inherits none of it.
verdicts.amendment: Name the estimand on the table: `flooded_reported` (what 311/alerts support) as the default target, with `flooded_observed` reserved for asset-event pairs carrying a wet-or-dry observation. Replace the binary with `label_state` in {positive, observed_negative, unlabeled}: observed_negative only where an in-radius sensor or gauge read below threshold for the whole window, unlabeled otherwise. 08 reports CSI/POD/FAR on the observed subset and PU-corrected or propensity-offset estimates on the rest, and never mixes them into one number. Replace the severity ordinal with the physical quantity plus provenance: `depth_mm` (nullable), `depth_source`, `depth_ci`, and a separate `confidence` field for source trust — never let a source-ordering masquerade as depth. State the split unit (event cluster), the clustered-SE convention, and the minimum event count for a reportable CSI; publish per-event CSI with an interval alongside the pooled number, since the two answer different questions when two events hold half the positive mass.

verdicts.reason: The storage half is reused wholesale from pipeline-09 and genuinely holds: plain Parquet Silver sorted by (source, ts), GeoParquet 1.1 for geometry only, EPSG:4326, TIMESTAMP_MICROS UTC. The time semantics do not. (i) 'Event-day defined in America/New_York (storms are local-day phenomena)' is asserted, not measured, and is false in the direction that matters: bucketing a COUNT threshold by local day splits an overnight storm across two buckets so neither fires, while the identical daytime storm fires. 24/99 subway flood events are first seen 00:00-05:59 local. (ii) The claim that hour-aligned windows join `silver/precip_cell_hourly` 'for free' is mechanically true and statistically misleading: the window is built from OBSERVATION timestamps, 311 `created_date` is the filing time not the incident time, and alerts fire when service is disrupted, after the water. The joined Cell-hours are systematically later than the raining hours and the +/-3h pad is smaller than the lag — Ida is the illustration, rain the evening of 09-01 with all alert events stamped 09-02. This depresses the precip signal the score depends on, in a way that will be misread as 'precipitation is a weak predictor'. (iii) Depth in mm and elevations in NAVD88 US ft with no named conversion point, in a project whose own map Notes carry a datum trap table, and with FloodNet publishing the same measurement in mm via the API and inches via Socrata `aq7i-eu5q`. (iv) The Storm Events `CZ_NAME` filter is a free-text pattern match — the exact failure the draft forbids two sections earlier ('descriptors must be enumerated, never pattern-matched', after the 8,700 'Flood Light Lamp' rows). NYC appears under both county-coded and zone-coded rows with names like 'Kings (Brooklyn)' and 'Richmond (Staten Is.)'. (v) CO-OPS: no choice stated between `hourly_height` (misses a 6-min surge peak between hours) and `water_level` (6-min but returns preliminary q=p for recent dates), no minimum duration or consecutive-reading rule for an exceedance, and no rule for gauge outages during the very events criterion (d) exists to catch.
verdicts.amendment: Keep pipeline-09's storage conventions verbatim. Replace the local-calendar-day trigger with a rolling 24h window ending each hour, evaluated in UTC, with the local day retained only as a display label. Add `obs_ts_kind` in {incident, report, alert} to every observation row and build event windows from forcing hours only (per D2), never from report timestamps. Name one conversion point: store `depth_mm` and `elev_ft_navd88` canonically with a single derived `sill_freeboard_mm` where they meet, converting FloodNet's Socrata inches at ingest. Replace the CZ_NAME string filter with FIPS county codes (36005/36047/36061/36081/36085) plus the enumerated NWS zone ids, and pin EVENT_TYPE to an enumerated set. State CO-OPS product = `hourly_height` for the historical spine cross-checked against `water_level` on candidate days, exceedance = >=2 consecutive readings above `nws_minor` via `datum=NAVD`, and record gauge gaps as explicit `coverage=missing` rather than an implicit non-event.

missing: FloodNet exceedance threshold and field: which of `depth_raw_mm` / `depth_filt_mm` (which silently zeroes everything under 10 mm) / `depth_proc_mm`, what mm cut, and what minimum duration. 'Depth exceedance' is the entire high-confidence truth tier and is left undefined; the field choice alone sets a hidden 10 mm threshold.

Whether to use FloodNet's own curated event table (`aq7i-eu5q`, 2,929 rows, `flood_start_time`/`flood_end_time`/`max_depth_inches` plus per-event depth profiles) instead of hand-rolling a threshold — never mentioned, and it is both lazier and more internally consistent than a bespoke rule.

How FloodNet's nightly 11:30pm baseline recalibration is handled — the depth-zero point drifts and is frozen mid-flood when the window's SD exceeds 5 mm, so 'depth' is relative to a moving reference — and the pre-Nov-2021 5-minute sampling era, which lowers detection probability for flash onsets during Ida specifically.

Which 311 timestamp defines the observation: `created_date` (filing time) vs `closed_date` vs `resolution_action_updated_date`, and how the filing lag between incident and filing is corrected before the window is drawn.

Which 311 geometry is trusted: `latitude`/`longitude` vs `incident_address` vs `intersection_street_1/2` vs `location_type`, and what happens to rows geocoded to a borough or ZIP centroid or missing coordinates — an intersection-centroid geocode plus a 100 m buffer clumps positives at intersections.

311 duplicate and re-open handling: the draft explicitly refuses to dedupe while making 'count-weighted presence' load-bearing, but never decides what to do with complaints closed as duplicates or with one puddle reported by several neighbours.
What 'count-weighted presence' actually is — a weight in the label, a severity input, or a feature. The label is stated as binary, so it currently has no consumer.
Observed-dry definition: FloodNet and CO-OPS below-threshold readings are the only uncontaminated negatives in the entire source set and are not used anywhere.

Prevalence and positives-per-event budget: no statement of how many positive asset-event pairs exist per asset class or per event class, so it is unknown whether CSI is estimable at all before the pipeline is built.

Minimum event count / power for event-held-out validation, and the clustered-standard-error convention — pipeline-10 already established 'errors clustered by wet event' and the flood label set inherits none of it.
Per-event weighting or capping so Sandy (a citywide polygon) and Ida (29 of 99 subway events) do not own the positive class.
Spatial blocking for validation splits: a 100 m buffer makes neighbouring bus stops and entrances near-duplicates, so event-held-out splitting alone still leaks within an event.

Asset-existence validity windows: labels for asset-event pairs where the asset did not exist at event time (new entrances, moved bus stops, closed stations) are spurious negatives across a 16-year table.
Label versioning / as-of snapshot: 311 is mutable and back-fills, so a re-run silently changes published CSI. Pipeline-09 already has the `pick_id = zip sha1` precedent and it is not applied here.
Precipitation-phase gate for the pluvial class: 19 of 57 criterion-(a) event-days are Dec-Mar, and pipeline-08's `t2m_c` and rain-not-snow convention already exist but are not used.

Day-of-week and seasonal reporting-rate correction for 311 — the largest measurable reporting structure in the data (weekend/weekday mean ratio 0.546, CI [0.474, 0.630]) is uncorrected while a non-existent era effect is corrected.
Event-class rules for the combinations left undefined: (b) AND (d), (c) AND (d), and event-days with no meteorological forcing at all.
Minimum-corroboration rule for criterion (b): one subway alert on a day with zero citywide 311 flooding complaints (2021-05-23) currently creates a full event-day for the whole asset universe.
Exclusion of alert boilerplate flood-reminder footers and flood-mitigation/planned-work rows — both already measured in `research/subway-flood-labels.md` and not applied in the spine.
What to do with system-wide alerts that name no station: they currently create an event that yields no station labels, so the largest events produce the fewest positives.

CO-OPS specifics: product choice (`hourly_height` vs 6-min `water_level`), exceedance duration / consecutive-reading rule, QC-flag policy (preliminary `q=p` vs verified), and gauge-outage handling during the events the criterion exists to catch.
Whether coastal criteria need a Jamaica Bay / Rockaway gauge, or an explicitly stated and flagged blind spot for one of the city's most flood-prone coastal areas.

Pre-2020 vs post-2020 spine comparability: pre-2020 has no `event_id`, different alert wording ('water condition' 66.7% vs 'flood' 21.5%), and no FloodNet — so any temporal split confounds a label-definition change with a model change.
Storm Events' own reporting drift and its county/zone spatial support: used as a spine criterion with no drift treatment, when the same objection was the stated justification for the 311 era split.
The named estimand: P(asset floods) vs P(a 311 report is generated). The entire meaning of the eventual CSI/POD/FAR turns on which one is being claimed, and neither is written down.

Expected annual count of criterion-(d) days and whether a nuisance minor-threshold exceedance at the Battery counts as a flood event at all — frequent, largely damage-free exceedances would silently dominate the coastal class with all-negative events.
Where the attachment-radius sweep runs (inside the CV fold vs on the evaluation set) and which number is reported as the headline.

verdicts.reason: Storage-convention misuse plus a fabricated field name. (1) `silver/flood_obs` is declared "Plain Parquet per pipeline-09 conventions" while carrying a `geometry/ref` column — pipeline-09 says GeoParquet 1.1 (SRID 4326, crs omitted) is required *on geometry tables*, and D6 restates that same rule, so D1 contradicts both 09 and D6. (2) `depth_mm` is not a FloodNet field. flood-03 §4 names three parallel fields served side by side for every reading: `depth_proc_mm` (recommended, heuristic-filtered), `depth_filt_mm` (<10mm zeroed), `depth_raw_mm`. `waterDepth` for NFIP is real (vault §2). (3) No `cell` key anywhere in the three-layer shape, though flood/map.md commits to reusing H3 res 8 wholesale and the pipeline map's whole rationale for this effort is that it "combines with the bus Gold at Cell-hour". (4) `ref/flood_events` is derived from `silver/flood_obs` and consumed by `gold/flood_labels` — pipeline-09 defines `data/ref/` as "small lookups, rebuilt whole" (grids, cells, zones, picks, calendar: all inputs). Putting a derived spine there makes the build DAG silver->ref->gold. (5) `gold/flood_labels` gets no partition key; 09's Gold convention is `month=YYYY-MM`. (6) Partitioning flood_obs by `source` alone means adding one month of 311 rewrites 2010-2026.
verdicts.amendment: `silver/flood_obs` partitioned `source=/year=`; geometry-bearing rows land as GeoParquet 1.1 (SRID 4326, crs omitted) per pipeline-09, or carry `lon`/`lat` DOUBLE plus a `geo_ref` STRING with the geometry in a sibling ref layer — a plain-Parquet table with a geometry column violates 09. Severity fields named exactly: `depth_proc_mm` (FloodNet's recommended field; `depth_filt_mm`/`depth_raw_mm` also exist, `depth_mm` does not), `waterDepth` (NFIP). Every row carries `cell INT64` (H3 res 8 of the observation point, or of the polygon/zone centroid) so the flood layer keys to `ref/cells`, to `silver/precip_cell_hourly`, and to the bus Gold. The event spine is derived over Silver, so it lands at `silver/flood_events`, not `ref/`. `gold/flood_labels` partitions `month=YYYY-MM` of `window_start` per 09's Gold convention.

verdicts.reason:
Two independent measured contradictions, either fatal on its own.

(i) Criterion (d) compares a NAVD88 series against STND thresholds. flood-05 §2 states the six stations' thresholds verbatim as "All in feet on Station Datum (STND)", the vault's Trap 1 repeats it, and flood/map.md's own Notes repeat it a third time. Testing a `datum=NAVD` series against `nws_minor` = 10.49 (Battery) or 22.89 (Kings Point) is off by that station's own offset — 6.06 ft at Battery, 17.09 ft at Kings Point. Consequence, quantified: at Battery the criterion effectively fires only above 16.55 ft STND (Sandy's peak was 17.329 STND / 11.266 NAVD88 per the vault, so Sandy passes by accident and essentially nothing else does); at Kings Point the effective bar becomes 39.98 ft STND, which never occurs. Criterion (d) as written yields ~1 coastal event-day in 16 years and disables the coastal/mixed classes it is supposed to create.

(ii) "Sandy=coastal" is refuted by the draft's own criterion. Measured live 2026-08-22 on the same union the draft used: 2012-10-29 = 97 street+highway complaints (2012-10-30 = 65). The 2010-2019 nearest-rank p99 over days with >=1 is exactly 97. So (a) fires for Sandy, and under "coastal if (d) fires without (a)" Sandy classifies as **mixed**. The classification of the single most important coastal event in the record turns on a one-complaint margin.

Also wrong, smaller: the quoted "96/day" is the *pooled* p99 and is neither era's threshold — measured per era it is 97 (2010-2019, 3,166 days with >=1) and 84 (2020+, 2,296 days). The stated rationale ("absorb report-rate drift") predicts the later threshold rises; it falls by 13. A live percentile is also not reproducible: it shifts as days accrue and retroactively re-labels history, which is exactly what pipeline-09 refuses elsewhere by freezing `ref/grids` with `coord_sha256`/`frozen_at`. And criterion (b) at ">=1" has no planned-work exclusion despite research §3 measuring 5/621 "flood protection/mitigation/barrier/resiliency" rows and §4 spot-checking boilerplate-footer matches; reproduced live, 2 of the 99 post-2020 subway `event_id`s are false (19148, a switch problem at 137 St-City College carrying a weekend flood-mitigation reminder; 21783, a person struck by a train), each manufacturing an event-day on an otherwise quiet date. Finally the +/-3h window pad is a free parameter that sets the label window D5 depends on, yet only D4's radii are sent to 08's sweep.
verdicts.amendment: (a) Absolute frozen thresholds, not live percentiles: `>= 97/day` for 2010-2019 and `>= 84/day` for 2020+ (nearest-rank p99 per era over the 5,462 days with >=1, measured 2026-08-22), stored with a `frozen_at` the way `ref/grids` freezes `coord_sha256`, so a refresh cannot re-label history. (b) unchanged, minus a measured exclusion: drop events whose only flood wording is planned-work or a status-footer reminder (research §3's 5/621 pattern; 2 of the 99 post-2020 subway event_ids). (c) unchanged. (d) Compare like to like: pull `datum=STND` and test against the published `nws_minor` (Battery 10.49, Kings Point 22.89), or convert each threshold by that station's own `datums.json` offset (Battery 6.06, Kings Point 17.09) before testing a NAVD series; never reuse 6.06 off-Battery. Class: take `FLOOD_CAUSE` from the Storm Events row where one exists — it publishes the pluvial/coastal cause directly (vault: 565 NYC flood rows with narratives and flood cause) — and fall back to flag co-occurrence only where it is absent. Record that Sandy fires (a) at 97 vs a 97 threshold and is therefore `mixed`; Ida stays pluvial. Send the +/-3h pad to 08's three-cutoff sensitivity sweep alongside the radii.

verdicts.reason: Trust tiers are sound and the FloodNet 2020-10+ start matches flood-03's measured earliest `date_deployed` (2020-10-05). Four problems. (1) "alerts 2012+" is a dataset-coverage date masquerading as a signal-coverage date: `3h5b-5ktz` starts 2012-10-02, but research §2's measured flood-keyword rows by year are 2013:1, 2014:14, 2015:26, 2016:87 — the alert flood signal is effectively 2016+, so the coverage flag overstates four years of a 16-year label window. (2) Alert station labels are promoted to label-grade while ticket 02 is `Status: open` and its own text says "The measured P/R decides whether alert labels are a first-class label source at station grain or a garnish" — the draft pre-decides an open ticket's outcome. (3) FloodNet is called high-confidence truth without the asymmetry: flood-03 §7 measures 430/440 sensors `mounted_over: sidewalk` and states outright that sensors sit on existing signposts rather than topographic lows and cannot detect roadbed flooding below curb height, plus nightly baseline recalibration drift and a live snow false-positive banner. FloodNet is a high-confidence positive and an unreliable negative — which is load-bearing for D5's tiered truth and for 08's CSI. (4) The FloodNet non-commercial NYU/CUNY Data Access License is never mentioned even though FloodNet is made label-grade. Missing sources are listed separately.
verdicts.amendment: Coverage flags state the flood-signal start, not the dataset start: alert flood coverage is effectively 2016+ (measured rows/yr 2013:1, 2014:14, 2015:26, 2016:87). Alert station labels are *provisional* label-grade, gated on ticket 02's measured P/R. FloodNet is a high-confidence positive and never a high-confidence negative (signpost mounting, 430/440 over sidewalk, below-curb blindness, nightly recalibration drift, documented snow false positives) — a FloodNet null is "not seen", not "dry". Add to the roster or explicitly reject: NYCT **Bus** flood alerts (665 post-2020 + 472 pre-2020 rows, more than Subway in both eras per research §2) as the street-grain label candidate; NFIP `dateOfLoss` as a fifth spine criterion (44,110 dated NYC claims 1978-2026, the only dense dated record covering the 2010-2016 hole); IEM Local Storm Reports and warning polygons as point-grain label-grade observations; FloodNet's Socrata event table `aq7i-eu5q` (2,929 rows, one per detected flood event, `flood_start_time`/`flood_end_time`/`max_depth_inches`, plus within-event depth-profile arrays) as the label-shaped path in place of a 10k-row-capped per-sensor API backfill — noting it reports **inches** while the API reports mm. Record the NYU/CUNY non-commercial license against any published artifact.

verdicts.reason: The dedupe half is exactly right and precisely sourced: `event_id` post-2020 / `status_id` pre-2020 matches research §5, and "19% of events gain flood wording late" matches the measured 80/99 at `update_number=0`. The 100 m 311 radius matches the vault's own step-2 recommendation. Gaps: (1) no CRS for the buffers — pipeline-09 requires buffers/areas in EPSG:32618 and geodesic-only where a distance feeds a metric; a 100 m ring computed in 4326 degrees is wrong by ~24% in the lon direction at 40.7N. (2) No rule for the ~2.4% of 311 rows with no lat/lon (vault: 97.6% populated), i.e. ~1,200 of the 50,605 SJ/SH rows silently vanish from a "count-weighted presence" attachment. (3) "alert station label -> that station's entrances directly" hides a one-to-many join: the extractor yields an everyday name, which must resolve through GTFS stop_id(s) to `complex_id` to `i9wp-a4ja`'s 2,120 entrances, and complex names like "149 St - Grand Concourse" fan out to several stop_ids. (4) FloodNet's 50 m ring inherits the D3 asymmetry — a hit is a positive, an absence is not a negative. (5) Pre-2020 `status_id` dedupe is asserted without its residual: research §5 measured 20 groups that are exact (date, header) duplicates covering 61/186 rows and timestamps repeating to the second within a group.
verdicts.amendment: Buffers computed in EPSG:32618 per pipeline-09; geodesic (`ST_DistanceSpheroid`) where a distance feeds a metric. State the drop rule and the count for 311 rows without lat/lon (~2.4%, ~1,200 of 50,605 SJ/SH). Alert attachment path written out: matched name -> GTFS stop_id(s) -> `complex_id` -> `i9wp-a4ja` entrances, one-to-many, owned by ticket 02's asset. FloodNet's 50 m ring is positive-only evidence. Record the residual after `status_id` dedupe (20 exact (date, header) duplicate groups over 61/186 pre-2020 subway rows).

verdicts.reason: The negatives framing is the best thing in the draft — "no report" not "dry", with tiered truth handed to 08, is straight out of the vault's step 3 and is right. But the severity ordinal is a category error. `max(FloodNet depth exceedance > HWM > alert station > 311 presence)` ranks *sources*, not *severities*: a 30-complaint 311 cluster within 100 m of an asset is not less severe than a single 10 mm FloodNet exceedance, it is less trusted. Calling one ordinal "severity tier" also contradicts D1's explicit "no cross-source normalization of severity" two paragraphs earlier. Separately, the negative universe is unbounded: `gold/flood_labels` is asset x event with no asset registry (ticket 06 is `open`), no class-balance statement, and no decision on whether negatives are materialized or implied — which matters because the draft's own measurement says station-grain labels are rare-event data (99 events over 36 first-seen days, reproduced live).
verdicts.amendment: Split the ordinal. `confidence_tier` = source precedence (FloodNet depth > HWM > alert station > 311 presence) — that is what the max() actually ranks, and it is the column 08's tiered truth wants. `severity` = only where a source measures it (`depth_proc_mm`, HWM `elev_ft` NAVD88, NFIP `waterDepth`), NULL for presence-only sources, which honours D1's no-normalization rule. Bound the negative universe: state the asset registry dependency (ticket 06, open), the row estimate, and whether negatives are materialized or implied — 2,120 entrances x ~55 events is 116K rows, but adding bus stops and street segments crosses 10M.

verdicts.reason: Everything in D6 that restates pipeline-09 is accurate (plain Parquet Silver, GeoParquet 1.1 for geometry tables, EPSG:4326, TIMESTAMP_MICROS UTC, mm for FloodNet-native depth, NAVD88 US ft for elevation, local event-day stored as UTC bounds). The one novel claim is false, and it is a rail misuse of exactly the kind that must be refuted rather than tweaked: "event windows hour-aligned with ceil_hour semantics so `ref/flood_events` joins `silver/precip_cell_hourly` for free." It is not free, three ways. (i) `precip_cell_hourly` is keyed **(src, cell, hour_end_utc)** (08 §4). An event window carries no cell, so an hour-only predicate cross-joins all 4,113 Cells per hour — 36.0M rows/yr on the other side. (ii) 08 mandates that consumers pin `src` explicitly and that srcs are never pooled in one fit (Pass2 measured at 0.86-0.92 of AORC); a 2010-2026 label table spans the src boundary by construction and D6 never mentions the pin. (iii) There is no precip spine for most of the label window: pipeline decision 02 scopes AORC to 2020-2025 history (08 uses it for the 2017-07..2024-09 backfill, 2025.zarr ending 2025-12-31T23:00Z), and `src=mrms` is deliberately ingested only from 2026-08-14T00:00Z with 2026-01-01..08-13 explicitly skipped. So labels from 2010-01-01 to roughly 2017 — and the 2026 gap — carry no precip features at all, which lands directly on ticket 08's exposure score. `ceil_hour` itself is used correctly (it maps a point into the hour-ending label (H-1h, H], so applying it to both bounds does enumerate the covering hours), but the resulting join is a range predicate, not the equi-join "for free" implies. Missing besides: no DST rule, though an America/New_York calendar day is 23 or 25 hours twice a year and pipeline-10 explicitly drops those two transition hours from its baseline.
verdicts.amendment: Pipeline-09 wholesale for the restatement (plain Parquet Silver, GeoParquet 1.1 on geometry tables, EPSG:4326, TIMESTAMP_MICROS UTC, buffers/areas in EPSG:32618); depth in mm where the source is native mm (`depth_proc_mm`), with an explicit conversion note for `aq7i-eu5q`'s inches; elevations NAVD88 US ft; CO-OPS thresholds stay STND unless converted per station. The precip join is NOT free: (i) every labelled asset and every event window carries an H3 res 8 `cell`, because `silver/precip_cell_hourly` is keyed (src, cell, hour_end_utc) and hour alignment alone cross-joins 4,113 Cells per hour; (ii) `src` is pinned explicitly at every read and srcs are never pooled (Pass2 0.86-0.92 of AORC), so the label table records which src covers which span; (iii) state the coverage gap plainly — no precip spine before AORC's ingested era (~2017; decision 02 scopes it 2020-2025) and none for 2026-01-01..08-13, so pre-spine labels carry NULL precip features and ticket 08 must hold them out rather than impute. `ceil_hour` maps a point to an hour-ending label ((H-1h, H]); applied to both bounds it enumerates covering hours correctly, so keep it but write the join as a range predicate on `hour_end_utc`. Event-day is America/New_York; name the two DST-transition days where that day is 23 or 25 hours (pipeline-10 drops those hours in its baseline).

missing: Cell key. The draft never assigns H3 res 8 to any observation, event, or label, though flood/map.md commits to reusing 'H3 res 8 Cell grain' wholesale and the pipeline map's stated reason for this effort is that it 'combines with the bus Gold at Cell-hour'. Without a cell the precip spine, the bus Gold, ref/cells, and ref/cell_zone are all unreachable.

Precip coverage for the label window. Labels start 2010-01-01; src=aorc is scoped 2020-2025 by pipeline decision 02 (used for the 2017-07..2024-09 backfill by 08, 2025.zarr ending 2025-12-31T23:00Z) and src=mrms is ingested only from 2026-08-14T00:00Z with 2026-01-01..08-13 deliberately skipped. Roughly seven years of labels have no precip features, and ticket 08's exposure score consumes them. Not acknowledged anywhere.

src pinning. 08's hard rule is that consumers pin exactly one src and that srcs are never pooled in one fit (Pass2 measured 0.86-0.92 of AORC). A 2010-2026 label table spans the boundary by construction; the draft never decides how.

NYCT Bus flood alerts. Research §2 measured 665 post-2020 and 472 pre-2020 bus flood-keyword rows — more than Subway in both eras, and explicitly noted as plausible because bus routes cross more street-level flood-prone locations. Neither adopted, tiered, nor rejected. For a project whose other half is buses at Cell-hour grain, this is the closest available street-segment label source.

NFIP as a spine criterion. D3 demotes it to covariate-only, and D2 omits it entirely, but the vault ranks NfipClaims #1 of eight for reconstructing NYC flood history: 44,110 dated NYC claims 1978-2026 with dateOfLoss. It is the only dense dated record covering 2010-2016, precisely where alerts are near-empty (2013:1 row) and FloodNet does not exist.

IEM Local Storm Reports (lsr.py, point lat/lon plus REMARK narrative, full NWS archive) and IEM warning polygons (watchwarn.py, is_emergency / damagetag CATASTROPHIC on Ida). Point-grain dated flood observations covering the pre-2016 hole. Not mentioned, not rejected — despite flood-05 §7 devoting a whole section to making watchwarn queryable (limitps=yes required, limit1=yes actively excludes CF).
NOAA Storm Events FLOOD_CAUSE. The vault records 565 NYC flood rows 'with narratives and flood cause'. D2 infers event_class from which flag fired instead of reading the published field.

FloodNet's label-shaped product aq7i-eu5q (2,929 rows, one per detected flood event: flood_start_time, flood_end_time, max_depth_inches, onset_time_mins, drain_time_mins, plus within-event depth-profile arrays at ~60s). The draft implicitly commits to a 10k-row-capped, per-sensor, date-chunked API backfill across 440 sensors instead. Also unmentioned: kb2e-tjy3 (479 rows) carries lowest_point_height_delta_inches, a per-sensor elevation offset absent from the live API and directly relevant to a depth threshold.

FloodNet exceedance definition. 'Depth exceedances' is used as a label-grade criterion with no threshold value, no field choice (depth_proc_mm vs depth_filt_mm's <10mm zeroing vs depth_raw_mm), no channel decision (API mm vs aq7i-eu5q inches), and no handling for the documented nightly 11:30pm baseline recalibration (the depth-zero point drifts, it is not a fixed installation constant), the snow false-positive warning, blips/boxes/complex noise, or the 254 mm/min rate-of-change filter.
FloodNet licensing. The custom NYU/CUNY non-commercial Data Access License Agreement plus the Mydlarz et al. (2024) citation requirement, unmentioned while FloodNet is promoted to label-grade.

Exact 311 descriptor literals. The draft's own rule is 'descriptors must be enumerated, never pattern-matched', but its enumeration literal is wrong: verified live, the descriptor is 'Sewer Backup (Use Comments) (SA)', not 'Sewer Backup (SA)'; catch basin is 'Catch Basin Clogged/Flooding (Use Comments) (SC)'. An exact-match enumeration on the draft's strings returns zero rows. Also undecided: the small flood-adjacent descriptors the four-descriptor set drops — 'Ready NY - Flooding' (271), 'Flooded' (46), 'RAIN GARDEN FLOODING (SRGFLD)' (45) — and that the ~8,700 'Flood Light Lamp' false positives are entirely a pre-2020 phenomenon (zero in 9qq5-d465).
Asset universe and class balance. gold/flood_labels is asset x event with no asset registry (ticket 06, open), no negative-materialization rule, no row estimate, and no Gold partition key.

Ticket 02 as a stated gate. D3 makes alert station labels label-grade before 02 measures precision/recall, though 02's own text says that measurement decides first-class vs garnish. The dependency is never declared.
DST. The event-day is defined in America/New_York, which is 23 or 25 hours twice a year; pipeline-10 explicitly drops the two transition hours from its hour-of-week baseline. No rule given.
Buffer CRS for the attachment radii (pipeline-09: buffers/areas in EPSG:32618, geodesic only where a distance feeds a metric) and the drop rule for the ~2.4% of 311 rows with no lat/lon.

NYC OEM prefiltered 311 flood layer (103,424 points, Jun 2018-Aug 2023) — the vault flags it as saving a rebuild of the descriptor filter over 22.6M rows. Not evaluated as a cross-check on the enumeration.

NOTE ON MEASUREMENT QUALITY (not a gap): every fresh number in the draft reproduced exactly against live SODA on 2026-08-22 — 50,605 union total, 5,462 days with >=1, median 4/day, nearest-rank p99 96 pooled, max 912 on 2025-10-30, the full top-day ordering (634 / 364 / 351 / 314 / 184 / 166), top-20 share 10.76% vs sewer backup's 5.73%, sewer-backup median 28/day and Ida 2,372 on 09-02, ~8,672 'Flood Light Lamp' rows, and 435 subway rows -> 99 event_id -> 36 first-seen days with Ida 29 and 2023-09-29 20. The failures above are reasoning and rail-reuse failures, not measurement failures.

verdicts.reason: Three tables are defensible, but the shape carries state that adds no decision, and one internal contradiction. Measured size of the whole observation universe: 50,605 (311 SJ+SH, verified) + 2,929 (FloodNet events, verified) + ~2,300 alert rows + a few hundred HWM + 1 Sandy polygon = under 60k rows total. Partitioning a 60k-row table by source produces ~8 tiny files for zero benefit and contradicts pipeline-09's sort-not-shard habit. `geo_kind` is derivable (ST_GeometryType) — a variant column shadowing the geometry. Per-source coverage flags on every event row are a static per-source date range repeated a few hundred times. And D1 lists NFIP `waterDepth` as a severity field in `flood_obs` while D3 says NFIP never becomes a label — the draft never says which sources actually land in the table.
verdicts.amendment: silver/flood_obs: one unpartitioned GeoParquet file, sorted (source, ts_utc). Columns: source, source_id, ts_utc, geom (mixed point/polygon in one GeoParquet column), depth_mm (nullable, only where the source measures depth), text (nullable, the alert/complaint string). No geo_kind (use ST_GeometryType), no partition dirs. It holds label-grade sources only (311 SJ/SH points, FloodNet events, alert station labels, USGS HWM, Sandy polygon); covariate sources (NFIP, sewer backup SA, catch basin SC, MyCoast) are read straight from their own tables by 08 and never enter flood_obs. ref/flood_events: event_id, day_start, day_end, window_start_utc, window_end_utc, and four boolean trigger columns by_311 / by_alert / by_storm / by_tide. Drop event_class and the per-source coverage flags: class is f(triggers) computed at read, and per-source coverage is six literal date ranges in one code constant (311 2010-01-01+, alerts 2012-10-02..2020-03-31 and 2020-04-28+, FloodNet 2020-11-16+, CO-OPS 1927+, Storm Events 1996+).

verdicts.reason: The spine as written cannot be built: criterion (d) is provably always-empty, the window rule is circular, and the class rule mis-labels coastal Storm Events rows. (d) says 'observed exceedance of NWS minor threshold ... NAVD88 series via datum=NAVD' — but floodlevels.json thresholds are published on STND (the map's own Notes say so: NAVD88 = 6.06 ft on STND; Battery nws_minor = 10.49). A NAVD series peaks near 4.5 ft, so nothing ever exceeds 10.49 and (d) never fires. The window rule ('union of contributing observation timestamps') needs attachment results that do not exist until after the spine defines the window. The class rule sends a Storm Events coastal-flood row (c) to 'pluvial' whenever (d) is silent. Separately, the thresholds in (a) are TBD: the draft quotes the union p99 (96) and then splits by era without giving either era number. Measured today: era p99 (over days with >=1 complaint) is 97/day for 2010-2019 (76ig-c548, 3,166 days, 28,538 rows) and 83/day for 2020-2026 (erm2-nwe9, 2,296 days, 22,067 rows); union p99 is 94.8, not 96. That p99 rule yields only 57 event-days in 16.6 years, and it is knife-edge on the canonical events: Sandy 2012-10-29 = 97 (passes only because the test is >=), Sandy day two 2012-10-30 = 65 (missed), Irene 2011-08-28 = 80 (missed). Criterion (d) is not the flood risk I expected, once fixed: Battery 2023 at the correct datum exceeds nws_minor on 3 days (02-28, 06-03, 11-22), 11 days at the 10.29 action level — so it adds a handful of coastal days a year, not hundreds.
verdicts.amendment: Event-day (America/New_York, tz-aware so DST 23/25h days convert correctly) if ANY of: (a) 311 count over complaint_type='Sewer' AND descriptor IN ('Street Flooding (SJ)','Highway Flooding (SH)') >= the era p95 — 37/day for 2010-2019 from dataset 76ig-c548, 29/day for 2020-2026 from erm2-nwe9 (the era split IS the dataset split; p95 catches Irene at 80 and both Sandy days, and yields 273 event-days vs p99's 57 — if 57 is what you want, say 97/83 and accept losing Irene); (b) >=1 subway-alert flood event (event_id post-2020 / status_id pre-2020, both 'flood' and 'water cond' phrasings); (c) NOAA Storm Events row with EVENT_TYPE IN ('Flash Flood','Flood','Coastal Flood') for the five boroughs; (d) CO-OPS hourly_height fetched with datum=STND at Battery 8518750 or Kings Point 8516945, compared directly to that station's own floodlevels.json nws_minor (Battery 10.49) — same datum on both sides, no arithmetic; chunk requests at <=365 days or the API 400s. Contiguous event-days merge. Window = [NY-midnight of the first event-day minus 3h, NY-midnight after the last event-day plus 3h], converted to UTC — hour-aligned by construction, no dependency on attachment. Class from the trigger flags: coastal if by_tide or the Storm Events row is Coastal Flood; pluvial if by_311 or by_alert or a Flash Flood/Flood row; mixed if both. GDELT stays out (agreed, no change).

verdicts.reason: Two problems. (1) 'FloodNet depth exceedances' names no threshold, no persistence rule, and no baseline handling, and routes the build through the raw /depth REST API — which caps at exactly 10,000 rows per call (silently truncating, per the repo's own research) and is covered by a custom NYU/CUNY non-commercial licence. NYC Open Data already publishes the detected events: dataset aq7i-eu5q, verified live today — 2,929 rows, 2020-11-16 to 2026-08-11, one row per detected flood with flood_start_time, flood_end_time, max_depth_inches, duration_above_4/12/24_inches and the full 60s depth profile. That is the label-grade source, pre-thresholded by FloodNet's own detector, public NYC Open Data, one call. There is no threshold left to invent. (2) Alert station labels are declared label-grade before ticket 02 has measured the extractor's precision — the draft is spending evidence it has not collected, and 02's whole stated purpose is to decide 'first-class label source or garnish'.
verdicts.amendment: Label-grade: 311 SJ/SH points; FloodNet flood events from Socrata aq7i-eu5q (NOT the raw /depth API; join geometry on sensor_id to the DEP FloodNet sensor-location dataset, since aq7i-eu5q carries sensor_name/sensor_id and no coordinates; convert max_depth_inches * 25.4 to store mm, the summaries are inches while the raw API is mm); USGS high-water marks; Sandy inundation polygons (that event only); and alert station labels CONDITIONAL on ticket 02 measuring precision >= 0.90 on its hand-labeled sample — below that they drop to covariate/garnish and D5's source mix loses a member. Spine-only and covariate-only lists unchanged. Coverage note to add: alerts have a real hole 2020-04-01..2020-04-27 between the two Socrata datasets (3h5b-5ktz ends 2020-03-31, 7kct-peq7 starts 2020-04-28), and the Socrata tail stops 2026-06-29 while the archiver's alert capture starts 2026-08-16.

verdicts.reason: 'Defaults, sensitivity-swept in 08's validation' is a hand-wave that ticket 08 cannot absorb: 08 is Blocked by 01, so 01 must ship a fixed number or nothing downstream can be built. Four different radii (100/100/50/contains) is a four-knob table with no evidence behind the differences — a knob per source is exactly the state that adds no decision. Worse, 'FloodNet sensor -> its own street segment/Cell' presumes ticket 06's still-open question of whether street segments survive as a first-class asset, so the rule cannot be implemented today. And the radius rule is undefined for the non-point half of the asset universe (Cells are polygons; '100 m from a Cell' means nothing).
verdicts.amendment: One constant: RADIUS_M = 100, geodesic (pipeline-09), applied identically to every point-geometry label source (311, HWM, FloodNet sensor). Point asset attaches if ST_DistanceSphere(asset, obs) <= RADIUS_M. Cell-grain asset attaches if the observation's h3 res-8 index equals the Cell (no radius). Polygon source (Sandy) attaches by contains for point assets, by intersects for Cells. Alert station labels attach to that station's entrances and the station point directly, no radius. Say nothing about street segments — 06 decides whether they exist. The sweep is a named build item in 08 over the grid {50, 100, 200} m, reported as a CSI table; 100 m is the shipped default until that table says otherwise. Add: 311 rows with null or (0,0) coordinates are dropped, and the build reports the dropped fraction (do not geocode from incident_address).

verdicts.reason: The severity tier is a pure function of the source mix — max() over a fixed source ranking — so it stores zero information beyond the column sitting next to it, and it bakes a source-confidence opinion into the table under the name 'severity' (a 311 report during Ida and a 311 report on a nuisance day get the same tier; a 3-inch FloodNet event outranks a 20-inch alert closure). Delete the derived column, keep the inputs. Separately, 'negatives are asset-event pairs with no attached observation' materializes the full cross product: ~20k assets (2,120 entrances + stations + ~15k bus stops) x 57-273 events = 1.2M-5.5M rows, of which the positives are a few thousand, and every rebuild of ticket 06's asset registry invalidates the whole table.
verdicts.amendment: gold/flood_labels holds attached (positive) pairs only: asset_id, event_id, source_mix (sorted source string or bitmask), n_311, max_depth_mm (nullable, FloodNet only), first_obs_utc. No flooded column (presence is the label), no severity_tier. Negatives are generated where they are consumed, as one anti-join: ref/assets CROSS JOIN ref/flood_events LEFT ANTI JOIN gold/flood_labels. Keep the draft's honesty line verbatim — an absent pair is 'no report', not 'dry' — and keep tiered truth in 08.

verdicts.reason: Reusing pipeline-09 wholesale is right and needs no re-deciding. Two loose ends. The 'joins silver/precip_cell_hourly for free' claim is not free: precip is keyed on hour_end_utc, an event window is a range, and the draft never says whether window_start is an hour-start or an hour-end value — a builder guesses, and a one-hour offset silently misaligns every precip feature. And the NAVD88 US ft elevation sentence belongs to ticket 07: no table in D1 stores an elevation, so it is scope the label ticket does not own.
verdicts.amendment: Replace the join sentence with the expansion: window_start_utc and window_end_utc are both hour_end values (ceil_hour semantics, matching pipeline-08's key); the event-to-precip join is an explicit event_hours expansion, generate_series(window_start_utc, window_end_utc, INTERVAL 1 HOUR) joined on (src, cell, hour_end_utc). Drop the NAVD88 elevation line from this decision (07 owns it). Keep: plain Parquet, GeoParquet 1.1 for geometry tables, EPSG:4326, TIMESTAMP_MICROS UTC, depth in mm. Add: the event-day is computed with a tz-aware America/New_York localize, not a fixed UTC offset (DST days are 23/25 hours).

missing: Dataset ids and the exact descriptor whitelist. The draft says 'descriptors must be enumerated, never pattern-matched' and then never enumerates them. Verified today: the 2010-2026 union needs TWO datasets (76ig-c548 for 2010-2019, erm2-nwe9 which is now titled '311 Service Requests from 2020 to Present' and whose earliest row is 2020-01-01), and the filter is complaint_type='Sewer' AND descriptor IN ('Street Flooding (SJ)','Highway Flooding (SH)'). The draft's covariate strings do not match the data: the real values are 'Sewer Backup (Use Comments) (SA)' and 'Catch Basin Clogged/Flooding (Use Comments) (SC)'.

Which sources actually land in silver/flood_obs. D1 lists NFIP waterDepth as a severity field; D3 says NFIP is never a label. A builder cannot tell whether covariate-only sources are in the table, in their own tables, or nowhere.

FloodNet event geometry. aq7i-eu5q carries sensor_name and sensor_id but no lat/long — the location join (which dataset, which key, and the known trailing-space quirk in a FloodNet field noted in research/flood-03-floodnet.md) is undecided, and without it FloodNet labels cannot attach to anything.

NOAA Storm Events access and filter strings. No ticket covers it (03 = FloodNet, 04 = stormwater, 05 = tide). Needed: the file path (NCEI bulk CSV per year), and the exact CZ_NAME/CZ_TYPE values for the five boroughs — county-coded rows and zone-coded rows use different name strings, which is precisely the trap the draft's one-line 'CZ_NAME filter' waves at.

USGS high-water marks and the Sandy inundation polygon. Both are declared label-grade in D3 and neither has a verified endpoint, coverage window, or licence anywhere in the map's decisions. HWM in particular needs its date range known before 'labels table starts 2010-01-01' means anything.

event_id format and rebuild determinism. gold/flood_labels references event_id, so a non-deterministic id (a sequence number) breaks every downstream table on rebuild. Decide the format (first event-day as an ISO date string is the lazy stable choice) and state that the spine is rebuilt from scratch and idempotent.

Minimum-evidence rule for an event. May an event exist with zero attached label-grade observations?
